audience.notes: Australian couple in their 30s, AUD 150K+, planning a multi-day Bali wedding for 60 to 150 guests rather than an elopement. Adapted top two fears: (A) 'we pay for a polished package and discover the real cost and work sit outside it: guest rooms, transfers, a wet-season plan, service charges, extra events' and (B) 'managing suppliers and a large guest group in another country from Australia, with nobody accountable if the day slips'. Paying parent (advisory): clear, itemised quotes and knowing what the money buys. Anti-persona: the SERP is 'packages from', 'under AUD 10K' and elopement threads; do not echo it, no price-tier lists, no 'cheapest' framing.

payload.search_intent: Commercial investigation. Ranking pages are listings and price lists; the reader wants to know what a package actually covers and how to judge one.
payload.angle: The buyer's guide to Bali wedding packages for a couple planning a full wedding week: what a package is built to cover, the items it rarely includes, the legal side in two routes, a method to compare packages line by line, the questions that expose gaps, and the point where a bespoke plan run by a Wedded Advisor serves a larger guest list better than any set package. Quality and certainty, not price.

outline.h2: What a Bali wedding package usually covers
outline.answers: The categories a package is built around, so the reader knows what they are buying. Categories only, no venue or price lists.
must_include: Use 'bali wedding packages' in the first 100 words and in this H2 or its intro sentence.

Direct answer in the first 60 words: a package bundles a set of ceremony and reception elements for a fixed guest number and time window; what it includes varies by provider and must be read line by line.

Category list (as categories, never as one provider's list): ceremony site and set-up, reception space and time window, food and drink tiers, styling and florals, on-day coordination, basic audio, sometimes photography, a celebrant for a symbolic ceremony, and sometimes a room or two for the couple.

Three package types in one short table: resort or hotel package (venue's in-house team), planner package (a planner bundles suppliers), villa package (private villa plus planner). Columns: who builds it, what it tends to bundle, where control sits. No prices, no names.
One line: an 'all inclusive' label describes the bundle, not the whole wedding week (secondary keyword, natural use).

outline.h2: What Bali wedding packages rarely include
outline.answers: The invisible work and costs that sit outside a package. Main gap; addresses fear A.
must_include: Checklist or table of items commonly outside the package, framed as 'check whether yours includes': guest accommodation and room blocks; airport and venue transfers for guests; wet-season back-up space and its hire; welcome dinner, pre-wedding events and recovery-day brunch; extra hours beyond the time window; overtime for suppliers; vendor and crew meals; service charge and government tax (confirm current rates from an official or venue source, or write 'check whether quoted prices include service and tax'); premium drinks beyond the tier; legal paperwork and certificate costs; guest gifts and signage; travel and accommodation for imported suppliers.

Room blocks and transfers as the largest invisible job for a 100-guest week: hold dates, release dates, attrition, ground transport between villas and venue (no figures unless sourced from our own pages).
No competitor inclusions or prices; this list is general planning knowledge, not a paraphrase of any ranking page.
Link /destination-wedding-packages with a descriptive anchor, e.g. 'how our destination wedding packages are built'.

outline.answers: Which of two routes the couple is on, in a short section with links out. Not a legal guide.
must_include: Two routes in two short paragraphs or a two-row table: (1) marry legally in Australia, then a symbolic ceremony in Bali with no legal effect; (2) a legal Indonesian wedding in Bali, which involves religious and civil registration steps and Australian documents (research facts only from official sources: Smartraveller, Australian Consulate-General in Bali, Indonesian civil registry).
State that a package's 'ceremony' is usually symbolic; check whether any legal service is included and who provides it.

Route 1 links /expert-advice/weddings-abroad-where-can-you-legally-get-married (descriptive anchor). Recognition back home links /expert-advice/overseas-marriage-certificate (descriptive anchor, not the exact keyword).
House line: requirements change; confirm with official sources for your own passports.
No fees, day counts or document lists unless the research pack sources them officially. Mark gaps [[NEEDS: research answer]]. Full legal detail belongs to a later cluster spoke; do not expand here.

outline.h2: How to compare Bali wedding packages
outline.answers: A method to compare two or three packages like for like.
must_include: Ask every provider for an itemised quote in one currency, with the exchange basis stated and whether service and tax are included.

Comparison grid the reader can copy: inclusions by category, guest number the price is built on and the per-guest rate above it, time window and overtime, wet-season plan (named indoor or covered space, decision time, cost), supplier list and who contracts them, payment schedule and cancellation terms.
Guest numbers: packages are priced for a base guest count; for 80 to 150 guests the add-ons often change the comparison (say this as guidance, no figures).
Wet season: name the months only from a sourced climate reference (BMKG or a recognised climate source); the plan matters more than the forecast.
Currency line: packages are often quoted in USD or IDR; compare in AUD on the same date. No conversion figures in copy.

outline.h2: Questions to ask before you sign
outline.answers: A short list of questions that expose gaps.
must_include: 8 to 10 questions as a numbered list, e.g. What is excluded? Is service and tax in the price? What happens if it rains, and who decides when? Who is our on-day contact and how many events do they cover? Which suppliers are fixed and which can we bring? What are the overtime and noise curfew rules? Who handles guest rooms and transfers? What is the payment schedule and cancellation policy? Is any legal ceremony service included?
Do not repeat the comparison grid; questions only.

outline.answers: The point where a set package stops fitting a larger wedding week, and what end-to-end planning by a Wedded Advisor handles. Addresses fear B.
must_include: Signals: more than one event across several days, a guest list above the package's base, a private villa or exclusive-use estate, cultural or multi-faith ceremonies, imported suppliers, a specific look the in-house team does not offer.

What the Wonderland Concierge and a Wedded Advisor coordinate (wording from brand-profile only): shortlist and contracts, room blocks, guest transfers, wet-season plan, run sheet across events, one point of contact. No guarantees on dates or outcomes.
One real-wedding line, optional: a multi-day Bali wedding from our live real-weddings (e.g. /real-weddings/australian-couple-bali-toni-jay-destination-wedding) once added to link-map.
Links: /destinations/asia/bali (descriptive anchor, e.g. 'our Bali wedding destination guide'), /wonderland-concierge. Soft CTA here.
Bespoke is not framed as 'better' for everyone; a package suits a smaller, single-day celebration. No judgement.
